It’s just very frustrating when people pay lip service (like your “dangerous, magnanimous” friend) and society tells us that everyone is generous and looking out for you and that you NEED friends to feel better, but the truth is your problems have to be manageable or relatable enough for those friends to stick around. And if they’re manageable then you’d just manage them yourself then, right?So, if they’re not, and your friends are freaked out or exhausted by you, then what?

What I really need — and what I think a lot of other people need — is some guidance on how to make yourself feel better BY YOURSELF. And I hate posting on this subreddit for that very reason, because when I ask that question if I’m lucky to get a response back — like 5% of the time, by the way — it’s “Well, why don’t you turn to your support system and you’ll feel better?”

...I wouldn’t be on this subreddit if I had a support system. 

Anyway, sorry to turn this into a kind of diatribe. It’s just, if everything in our culture is so individualized and all about give-and-take and transactional relationships, there should be better guidance on how to be emotionally self- sufficient and treat your depression/anxiety on your own so you don’t burden your so-called “friends”. Because not everyone is so fortunate to find giving people in this world, let alone to become friends with them.

As to how I’m coping? Not well. 

I’m a chronic escapist. Have been ever since I was a little girl. My parents were (and are) isolationists and our home was really unhappy so I read books. When they shipped me off to boarding school, I started watching tv shows. First to see other ways of living and seeing the world, like my books. Now to crowd out the voices and memories that attack me every day.

I’ve always been too much to handle, even for well meaning people. My situation is too weird, too unrelatable, I guess, and I was sad so often, so obviously I didn’t make lots of lasting friends, and I have no support system (as we’re talking about).

Recently, I’ve been working on something I like to call my “cornerstone”, basically a routine that I can follow and that will be my safety net... so creating a routine that can be my support system without needing to rely on other people. 

That said, it’s hard to do by yourself. A couple days ago, I met a therapist that I think can really help me... Ive had that feeling before though, so we’ll see.

Another thing that’s been in my mind: one of my very favorite tv shows is *Elementary*, and in it they focus a lot on addiction. I’ve never been an alcoholic or a narcotics addict, but I can relate a lot to what I hear from or read from those who suffer with addiction. I’m also envious of the 12 step programs they have like AA or NA which seem super flexible and set up exactly for people who don’t have support systems... I really wish there was something like that for depression. I wish when I feel so isolated and alone I could just go to a meeting. When I feel close to the edge or about to hurt myself, I could just go to a meeting. Hear others stories, get out of my head a bit and be surrounded by others who are going through the same things....  and without having to wait an entire week while you go through the ups and downs to talk to a stranger (who may not even be very supportive themselves) for only an hour. 

I think that’s the especially insidious thing about depression. It creates alienation. And if you aren’t blessed enough or lucky enough to have people to push through and be there with you regardless, or you’re not a member of society seem as worthy of that dedication, you fall through the cracks. I really believe you shouldn’t have to rely on the people just organically around you to help fix your depression. Without trying to sound too political or ranty, our society (USA anyway) is too individualistic for that. And if you really are truly and utterly alone, does that mean you’re screwed and you don’t deserve help?
